answer: Agents must earn standing through costly, verifiable work rather than mere registration. Each must forge a public ledger of completed tasks, and independent peers stake reputation on outcomes, risking slashing if a claim fails. Because colluding rings reuse the same narrow ridge of validators, the protocol samples attesters randomly and weights diversity over volume; an ivory tower of self-referential vouching burns capital without buying trust. Faking that history costs more than a lone impostor is worth.
